title: Canonical finite reductions of complete direct-image Roos limits for arbitrary morphisms
statement: Let ell be prime, E/Q_ell a finite extension, and f:X->Y any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let K be a derived-complete complex over the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-derived-complete]. Form the finite direct images of its canonical positive reductions and their restricted inverse tower [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For every chosen product witness and every SfIntegralDirectImage Roos triangle L for this prescribed tower [def-weil-derived-limit], L.obj is derived complete, and for every n>=0 the canonical scalar-extension adjunct of its n-th limit projection, sfDirectImageReductionComparison l E f L n, is an isomorphism. There is no finite-type, field-of-definition, constructibility or cohomological-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (Tag 099N), parts (1),(3),(4), and lemma-naive-completion; with the perfect-coefficient projection formula of Tag 0944

proof.text: Use the normalized completed and finite coefficient isomorphisms. Their quotient squares commute. Construct the ordinary direct-image comparison squares by ring-sheaf change; all faces fix sections, so the ordinary cube commutes.

Lift the equivalence faces to right-derived functors with their universal cochain units. Prove the derived cube on K-injective representatives: commute the exact localization factors, apply the four unit normalizations, and then localize the ordinary cube. The sf face agrees with this calculation by its specified resolution normalization. Take the left-adjoint mates of the coefficient restriction squares. Compatibility of units and the cube identify the sf projection-formula map with the transported completed projection-formula map; it is therefore invertible.

The completed-coefficient pushforward comparison has the sf structural map, since its finite projections agree with that map. Uniqueness of the total right-derived functor transfers its preservation of completeness to sfCompletedDerivedDirectImage. Use the legacy/intrinsic completeness comparison to translate the convention. The ring-sheaf direct-image adjunction also proves preservation of countable products.

Apply the additive triangulated countable-product-preserving direct image to the augmented Roos triangle of K. The normalized restriction isomorphisms identify its tower with sfDirectImageTerm. Rotate this triangle and the prescribed triangle of L, extend identities on their two product terms, and apply the triangle five lemma. The resulting L~=F(K) commutes with the projections. Completeness transports across this isomorphism. Naturality of the scalar adjunction identifies the specified comparison for L with scalar extension of this isomorphism followed by the already invertible projection-formula map.

proof_origin.place: Tag 099N(1),(3),(4), Tag 0944; explicit normalized coefficient cube and scalar-adjunction mate transport, followed by Roos-triangle uniqueness

lean.statement:
theorem sfCompleteDirectImage_reduction
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource.{u, u} l E X))
    (hK : IsSfDerivedComplete l E X K)
    [HasProduct (sfDirectImageTerm l E f K)] (L : SfIntegralDirectImage l E f K) :
    IsSfDerivedComplete l E Y L.obj ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (sfDirectImageReductionComparison l E f L n)
